timeline: If you stood in Gifu Prefecture in 1891, the earth would horizontally shift eight meters in seconds. What caused the giant split?
Eighty kilometers of surface faulting ripped open the earth.
Horizontal shifts reached up to eight meters in places.
Scientists of that era believed subterranean explosions or underground magma caused the disaster.
But professor Bunjiro Koto proved sudden fault slip created the surface breaks.
Gray-Milne-Ewing seismographs pegged the shock before needles went off scale.
More than three thousand aftershocks rattled the region over fourteen months.
This largest inland earthquake in Japanese history launched modern seismology.
You assume earthquakes only shake the ground...
